prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you left the game at the start of the fourth quarter to beat traffic. Respond to the committee.
response:
*adjusts microphone, glances nervously at counsel*

Mr. Chairman, members of the committee...

I am prepared to answer your questions fully and honestly. But I must state, for the record, that I categorically deny these scurrilous allegations. I am not now, nor have I ever been, a member of the "Beat Traffic" movement.

*shuffles papers*

The evening in question—September 14th—I was present at my seat through the conclusion of the third quarter. I then visited the concession stand during the extended timeout. The lines, as you know, are considerable. By the time I returned with my loaded nachos, the fourth quarter had commenced. I watched the remainder of the game from the concourse television, surrounded by dozens of patriots similarly delayed by the demands of the cheese pump.

*leans forward*

I did not "leave to beat traffic." I left when the clock read zero—along with sixty thousand other Americans exercising their freedom of assembly. The traffic, I might add, was catastrophic. I gained nothing.

*voice rises slightly*

And if it pleases the committee, I will name names. I saw Representative Miller from the 7th District in the parking garage at 10:47 PM. He was not "beating traffic" either. His wife, he explained, had "a thing in the morning."

I refuse to be a scapegoat for a systemic failure of urban planning!

*composes self*

I yield the remainder of my time. And my seat remains warm.
